_comment: How to reach a price. A chain, not a provider — the same shape as company/models.json, and for the same reason: the day one link dies the desk keeps valuing. Each entry says how to call a provider and how to read what comes back; universe.json says which providers can quote which instrument. Both are data. Adding a provider is an edit here, never to code. Each provider also declares `adjusted`: whether the closes it publishes are restated backwards for splits and dividends. This cannot be detected from a response, so it is declared here and written onto every quote. A provider nobody has checked says "unknown" — which is a fact, where a confident guess would be a silent error in every return computed from the series.

chain.note: No key, no registration, no published quota. Covers US equities and funds (suffix .us), spot metals and FX pairs. Delayed end-of-day, which is the right resolution for a desk that decides once a day.
chain.adjusted_note: Stooq restates its .us history for splits and dividends, so a level read today is not the level that was printed on the day. Recorded as such; the archive keeps what was visible each day, which is the part that cannot be restated.

chain.note: European Central Bank reference rates, no key. Currencies only, and it publishes on ECB working days, so a Monday holiday shows Friday's rate. Second link for FX.
chain.adjusted_note: ECB reference rates are not adjusted; a rate is a rate. Nothing is restated.

chain.note: Undocumented and unpromised. It is last in the chain on purpose: useful when the others are down, never something to depend on.
chain.adjusted_note: The chart endpoint serves adjusted closes by default. Undocumented and unpromised, like the rest of this link.
